title: Psychological Safety Playbook for Release Debriefs (working draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight working playbook to make cross-functional release, canary, and A/B debriefs safer, more useful, and less punitive. Focus is on: fast signal capture, learning, restoring trust, and operational fixes — with explicit psychological-safety practices to avoid blame spirals.

Audience
Primary: release stewards, product owners, oncall/ops, SRE, solutions engineering, and customer success leads who will participate in post-release review rituals. Secondary: Eng managers and execs who review summary outputs.

Why this exists (short)
- We run many progressive exposure experiments (small cohorts, staged activation, metric-driven A/B tests) and sometimes things go sideways quickly.
- Traditional postmortems skew towards root-cause hunting and assignment; that scares engineers from surfacing near-misses and subjective signals.
- This doc proposes concrete ceremony language, a rapid-run debrief template, and a simulation matrix to practice 'safe stop' and 'revert-to-fallback' decisions.

Core principles (working list)
- No-blame framing: meetings start with a short read by the steward using neutral language (see sample scripts below).
- Psychological safety check: quick round where participants can say 'I need support' or 'I observed X' without having to explain details in public.
- Fast fixes prioritized over perfect root cause: we triage to shipping fixes and mitigations first, then schedule deeper RCA tasks.
- Shared ownership: designate an action owner but not a single-person accountability for the entire rollout.
- Signal-first: collect telemetry, human reports, and UX artifacts before hypothesis-driven hunt.

Quick ceremony template (15-40m depending on severity)
1) Open (2m) — steward reads: "We ran X across Y cohort. We observed Z. Our goals for this meeting are to capture what happened, make a small set of fast actions, and decide what to monitor. We are aiming for learning, not blame."
2) Psychological-safety check (2m) — round-robin single-sentence statements: "I observed..." or "I need help with..." (facilitator notes if anyone declines).
3) Evidence package (5-10m) — steward shares telemetry snapshot + relevant traces: latency/5xx, model drift signals, cost anomaly, UX screenshots, subset of flagged responses.
4) Quick decisions (5-10m) — categorize into: Immediate stop/fallback; Soft throttle; Continue+monitor. Use the decision matrix below.
5) Fast action list (5m) — 3 actions max for the next 24–72 hours with owners and SLAs.
6) Longer work (assign as tickets) & learning notes (2m) — agree on deeper RCA owner and timeline.
7) Close: reiterate appreciation, invite private follow-up if needed.

Decision matrix (steering heuristics)
- Severity axes: customer impact (none/low/high), safety/regulatory risk (none/low/high), infra/cost impact (none/low/high), probability of recurrence (low/medium/high).
- Quick rule examples (heuristic, not policy):
  - Safety/regulatory = high => STOP exposure immediately and escalate to Legal + Security.
  - Customer impact = high and probability of recurrence medium/high => fallback to previous stable model variant and throttle new traffic to 0–5%.
  - Cost spike without user-visible harm => enable cost-rate limiting/budget guardrails and monitor billing dashboards; schedule optimization RFC.

Sample language (scripts)
- Slack open channel: "release-ops: quick heads-up — experiment X with cohort=beta is showing elevated hallucination-rate. Stand-up debrief in 15m in #zoom-link. Objective: decide stop/monitor and capture 24–72h actions. No-blame."
- Steward read (verbatim): "We are here to learn. If you feel uncomfortable speaking in this room, DM me or the incident steward and we will follow up 1:1. The goal is to protect customers and reduce recurrence."

Post-debrief artifact (what to capture)
- One-paragraph summary (what/when/who/decision) — to be posted to Confluence and #release-ops.
- Evidence bucket: links to traces, Redwood Console screenshots, embedding drift charts, trace-ids, and sample user prompts.
- Action list with owners, JIRA/Linear ticket ids, and SLAs.
- Quick 'safety score' (0–5) assigned by steward to summarize residual risk.

Simulation matrix (practice scenarios to run quarterly)
- Scenario A: incremental latency degradation in Redwood Dedicated pool when shard X crosses 512 tokens; customer-facing timeouts increase from 0.1% to 2%. Objective: practice progressive throttle and routing to fallback model variant. Roles: steward, SRE oncall, model-owner, product PM.
- Scenario B: small A/B shows statistically significant regression in named-entity extraction for regulated region (EU) causing PII masking misses. Objective: safe-stop and compliance escalation. Roles: steward, legal, privacy, engineering.
- Scenario C: cost surge from runaway reranking loop in a client integration (third-party webhook loop). Objective: apply immediate quota clamp + notify CS. Roles: steward, infra eng, solutions-eng, customer success.

Workshop agenda for first-run (90 minutes)
- 0–10m: framing, roles, and psychological-safety primer (facilitator: product lead).
- 10–25m: walk through Decision matrix and sample steward scripts.
- 25–55m: run Scenario A (tabletop) with live telemetry snippets (engineer plays SRE).
- 55–75m: run Scenario B (escalation to Legal).
- 75–90m: capture improvements to the playbook and put next steps in-tact (owners).

Checklist: Pre-release steward prep (shallow, to reduce surprises)
- Confirm experiment cohort definitions and traffic slices (link to rollout config).
- Produce a one-page 'if alarm' plan: what counts as stop-condition, who to ping, rollback steps, and fallback endpoints.
- Confirm monitoring dashboards are annotated and alerting set with explicit thresholds.
- Pre-identify 2 cross-functional contacts (SRE, CS) who will get paged if threshold hit.

Risks & open questions (work-in-progress)
- How to enforce 'no-blame' language when execs push for names/owners during high-severity incidents? (proposal: steward acts as buffer, escalate only necessary info).
- Integrate with existing incident process vs separate lightweight debriefs for low-severity experiments. Need to map thresholds.
- How to store sensitive examples (user PII) while keeping debriefs readable by product & CS? (proposal: redaction + gated Confluence page with access list).

Concrete next actions (short list)
- [Maya] Draft standardized 1-paragraph post-debrief template and sample Slack messages (due 2025-10-10).
- [Ethan] Create a Confluence template with redaction checklist and evidence bucket fields (due 2025-10-07).
- [Sofia] Schedule first tabletop run with SRE and Legal (target 2025-10-16).
- [Liam] Wire up a minimal 'psych-safety' checkbox to the release creation UI in Redwood Console (prototype issue: RF-298).

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal)
- Want to capture anonymized 'near-miss' stories — maybe a monthly short digest to reward early reporting.
- Could borrow language from Google SRE blameless-postmortem template but keep it shorter.
- Keep the steward role light: rotate weekly across teams.

References
- Internal: https://confluence.redwood/internal/release-rituals (link to canonical rollout practices).
- Related ticket examples: PROJ-482 (experiment X rollback), RF-298 (console checkbox prototype).

-- end of working draft --

If you want: I can split this into a short Confluence template and a 1-page steward cheat sheet next.
